import * as THREE from 'three/webgpu'; import { Fn, If, instancedArray, instanceIndex, uint, atomicAdd } from 'three/tsl'; window.runExample = async function() { const output = document.getElementById('output'); output.innerHTML = 'Initializing...'; try { const renderer = new THREE.WebGPURenderer(); await renderer.init(); output.innerHTML = '✓ WebGPU ready\n'; // Input: array of numbers (some positive, some negative, some zero) const inputData = new Float32Array([ -5, 3, 0, 7, -2, 1, -1, 8, 0, 4, -3, 2 ]); // Expected output (positive numbers only) const expectedOutput = Array.from(inputData).filter(x => x > 0); output.innerHTML += `\nInput: [${Array.from(inputData).join(', ')}]\n`; output.innerHTML += `Expected: [${expectedOutput.join(', ')}] (${expectedOutput.length} items)\n`; // Create buffers const inputBuffer = instancedArray(inputData, 'float'); // Output buffer - allocate enough space for all inputs (worst case) const outputBuffer = instancedArray(new Float32Array(inputData.length), 'float'); // Counter buffer with atomic support (initialized to 0) const counterBuffer = instancedArray(new Uint32Array([0]), 'uint').toAtomic(); // Filter kernel: output only positive numbers const filterKernel = Fn(() => { const value = inputBuffer.element(instanceIndex); // Test: is this value positive? If(value.greaterThan(0), () => { // Get unique output slot using atomicAdd // atomicAdd returns the OLD value before incrementing const outputIndex = atomicAdd(counterBuffer.element(0), uint(1)); // Write value to our reserved slot outputBuffer.element(outputIndex).assign(value); }); })().compute(inputData.length); // Execute output.innerHTML += '\nRunning parallel filter...\n'; await renderer.computeAsync(filterKernel); // Read results const countBuffer = await renderer.getArrayBufferAsync(counterBuffer.value); const count = new Uint32Array(countBuffer)[0]; const resultBuffer = await renderer.getArrayBufferAsync(outputBuffer.value); const results = new Float32Array(resultBuffer).slice(0, count); output.innerHTML += `\nGPU output: [${Array.from(results).join(', ')}] (${count} items)\n`; // Verify (note: order might differ due to parallel execution) const sortedExpected = [...expectedOutput].sort((a, b) => a - b); const sortedResults = [...results].sort((a, b) => a - b); const isCorrect = sortedExpected.length === sortedResults.length && sortedExpected.every((v, i) => v === sortedResults[i]); if (isCorrect) { output.innerHTML += '\n✓ All positive numbers were filtered correctly!'; output.innerHTML += '\n (Order may differ due to parallel execution - that\'s OK)'; } else { output.innerHTML += '\n✗ Results don\'t match expected output'; } renderer.dispose(); } catch (error) { output.innerHTML += `\n✗ Error: ${error.message}`; console.error(error); } };
